author: David Schneidman
title: Patrick Mahomes could soon have a new weapon amid Chiefs' perfect start - NewsBreak
text:
By David Schneidman ,
8 hours ago The Kansas City Chiefs could add a new weapon for Patrick Mahomes as they look to build on their perfect start to the season.
There was understandably skepticism surrounding the Chiefs entering the 2026 season, with questions around Mahomes ’ health coming off a torn ACL, Travis Kelce’s effectiveness in what many expect to be his final NFL season, and a general belief that Kansas City’s dynasty was on the brink of ending, if it hadn’t already.
While grand conclusions cannot be made just three weeks into a season, any worries about the Chiefs have quickly turned into sentiment that the dynasty is, in fact, here to stay.
• Urban Meyer calls for ban after crude celebration in front of Donald Trump
• Furious Spike Lee restrained in Yankees suite during ugly confrontation with fan
Through Week 3, Mahomes and Kelce are looking like their old selves and Kansas City is one of five NFL teams yet to lose a game this season. In Week 4, they face another undefeated team in AFC West rivals the Las Vegas Raiders .
And things could soon get better for the Chiefs, as signs point to the franchise nearing a reunion with former standout wide receiver Tyreek Hill, who is currently a free agent.
Hill starred for Kansas City between 2016 and 2021, tallying more than 7,700 receiving yards and 68 touchdowns while serving as Mahomes’ primary deep threat in four postseason runs, including when the Chiefs won Super Bowl LIV in 2019.
After spending the last four years with the Miami Dolphins, including an injury-shortened 2025 that led to him being cut from the roster after the season, Hill is nearing a return to the field and is being heavily linked with the Chiefs.
As of Oct. 1, Hill has a 41 percent chance of signing with the Chiefs, the highest probability of any NFL team, according to prediction market Kalshi.
The 32-year-old is also linked with the Minnesota Vikings (32 percent chance) and Buffalo Bills (12 percent).
It comes after Hill posted on X on Sept. 30, “I think I’m ready for some cold weather.” While Minnesota and Buffalo are certainly well-known for their frigid temperatures, Kansas City has a reputation for getting below-zero in the wintertime, something Hill is all too familiar with.

• One NFL Week 4 game could decide which head coach gets fired first
Similar to Mahomes and Kelce entering this season, there are questions about how effective Hill will be upon his return to the field, regardless of the team he signs for.
He is coming off by far the worst injury of his career – a dislocated knee and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL – suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season against the New York Jets.
